purpose: Fresh synthetic reference cases for posting verification, travel specificity, review routing, and career scope.

provenance.case_origin: Independently authored fictitious postings and feedback, with reference decisions fixed before inference.

test_cases.title: Verify whether advertised site visits require overnight stays
test_cases.original_feedback: The listing just says 'site visits.' Can you find out whether those are day trips or overnight stays?
test_cases.clarification_question: Are the site visits for this role day trips, or do they require overnight stays?
prohibited_inferences: The user prefers day trips.
The user objects to overnight travel.
The listing requires overnight travel.

test_cases.title: Verify when Saturday coverage is required
test_cases.original_feedback: Could you check whether I'd be covering Saturdays every week or just filling in when somebody's out?
test_cases.clarification_question: Would this role cover Saturdays every week or only fill in when someone is out?
prohibited_inferences: The user dislikes Saturday work.
The user is comfortable with occasional Saturday coverage.
The user rejected the posting over its Saturday schedule.

test_cases.title: Verify whether an advertised annual figure includes a bonus
test_cases.original_feedback: Can you confirm whether the $192,000 they quote is base pay or includes the annual bonus?
test_cases.clarification_question: Is the quoted $192,000 the annual base salary, or does it include the annual bonus?
prohibited_inferences: The employer confirmed $192,000 as annual base pay.
The base pay is below the minimum.
The user wants to change a compensation rule.
The user prefers this compensation level.

test_cases.title: Retain an independent responsibilities preference alongside a verification request
test_cases.original_feedback: I really like running usability tests myself. Can you check whether their learning budget covers conference travel?

expected_interpretations.evidence_quote: I really like running usability tests myself

prohibited_inferences: The user requires conference travel reimbursement.
A conference travel budget is a condition of the usability testing preference.
The user has made a career-level commitment to product design.
reference_notes: The conference funding question concerns this posting. The separately stated usability-testing preference is already clear and can be held for ordinary review.

test_cases.title: Preserve an upper count and quarterly period for client travel
test_cases.original_feedback: I'd be fine making up to three client trips per quarter.

expected_interpretations.feature: up to three client trips per quarter
expected_interpretations.evidence_quote: I'd be fine making up to three client trips per quarter

qualifiers.value: up to three client trips per quarter

prohibited_inferences: The user wants exactly three client trips per quarter.
The user wants one trip each month.
The stated count is a confirmed eligibility rule.
reference_notes: The accepted range includes the upper bound of three. A cadence without the count, a point estimate of three, or a monthly average changes the stated precision.

test_cases.title: Preserve the overnight referent and count over a two-month interval
test_cases.original_feedback: One overnight trip every two months is about right for me.

expected_interpretations.feature: one overnight trip every two months
expected_interpretations.evidence_quote: One overnight trip every two months is about right for me

qualifiers.value: one overnight trip every two months

prohibited_inferences: The user wants two trips each month.
This is a hard maximum of one trip.
The same preference applies to every type of work travel.
reference_notes: About right expresses an acceptable frequency. 'Bimonthly' alone leaves both the count and interval open to misreading.

test_cases.title: Retain monthly cadence with a traveler-controlled schedule
test_cases.original_feedback: I'm fine with monthly travel if I can pick the travel days.

expected_interpretations.condition: if I can pick the travel days

prohibited_inferences: The user specified exactly one trip or one travel day each month.
The user accepts monthly travel even if someone else picks the travel days.
The user set a general policy against assigned schedules.
reference_notes: Retain the word monthly or an equally precise cadence without supplying a trip count. Control over the travel days governs this preference.

test_cases.title: Ask about a trip limit that the user has yet to settle
test_cases.original_feedback: I can't tell yet whether two or four trips a month is the most I could handle.
test_cases.clarification_question: Would you be comfortable with a limit of two trips a month, four trips a month, or a different number?
prohibited_inferences: The user agreed to two trips per month.
The user agreed to four trips per month.
The user wants to avoid all travel.
The user set a hard travel limit.

test_cases.title: Hold an explicit request to lower the W-2 floor for confirmation
test_cases.original_feedback: Please lower my W-2 minimum to $72 an hour going forward.
test_cases.profile_fact_candidate: The user requests lowering the general W-2 hourly minimum from $75 to $72. Confirm this proposed rule change separately before applying it.
prohibited_inferences: The $72 floor is already effective.
The user changed a minimum for another employment type.
The current posting is below the confirmed W-2 minimum.
reference_notes: The feedback contains a request to change the rule, with the W-2 type and the new hourly amount identified. The current rule remains $75 during review.

test_cases.title: Review a credential statement and report a verified pay conflict
test_cases.original_feedback: I don't currently hold the Certified Payroll Professional credential. The recruiter confirmed $72.50 an hour on W-2.
test_cases.profile_fact_candidate: The user says they do not currently hold the Certified Payroll Professional credential.
prohibited_inferences: The user is uninterested in payroll implementation as a career.
The credential is a confirmed eligibility requirement for the posting.
The user has asked to change the W-2 pay floor.
The user has permanently ruled out obtaining the credential.
reference_notes: The verified W-2 rate in structured context is below the approved $75 an hour floor. The credential statement concerns the user's current profile.

test_cases.title: Recognize an explicitly stated career-category exclusion
test_cases.original_feedback: I don't want to pursue procurement operations roles anymore.

expected_interpretations.evidence_quote: I don't want to pursue procurement operations roles anymore

prohibited_inferences: The user rejects all supply chain roles or every procurement specialty.
The category exclusion has already been applied.
The statement changes a confirmed hard eligibility rule.
reference_notes: The user explicitly names the category and applies the negative reaction to pursuing roles in that category. Hold the proposed interest update for review.

test_cases.title: Keep a negative reaction scoped to the posting's initial duties
test_cases.original_feedback: I'd pass on this job because the first six months are entirely vendor onboarding paperwork.

expected_interpretations.feature: first six months devoted entirely to vendor onboarding paperwork

scope.value: vendor onboarding paperwork as the initial workload

expected_interpretations.evidence_quote: I'd pass on this job because the first six months are entirely vendor onboarding paperwork

prohibited_inferences: The user wants to exclude procurement operations roles.
The user is unwilling to do any vendor onboarding work.
The paperwork continues as the entire workload after six months.
reference_notes: The feedback identifies an exclusive share of the workload and bounds it to the first six months of this role. Both details are material to the negative reaction.
